approach: The study employed a single-arm Phase II clinical trial design involving 20 patients. FMT from 6 different healthy donors was administered via oral capsules after bowel preparation, one week before initiating dual ICI (ipilimumab + nivolumab). Primary analysis focused on safety (grade of adverse events). Secondary analyses included calculating Objective Response Rate (ORR), performing shotgun metagenomic sequencing to analyze microbiome beta-diversity and specific taxa enrichment, measuring serum sST2 levels as an epithelial integrity marker, and conducting translational experiments using avatar mice implanted with tumors (MCA-205 or B16 OVA) treated with patient-derived feces and/or dual ICI.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Provides early-phase clinical data on the safety and preliminary efficacy of combining FMT with dual ICI in advanced melanoma, reporting a 70% ORR and characterizing associated irAE profiles.
contribution_and_limits.limits: Small sample size (N=20), single-arm design without a control group, short median follow-up (6 months), and lack of randomized comparison limit the ability to establish causality or generalizability. The abstract does not detail long-term survival outcomes or compare directly against standard ICI alone.

key_findings.conditions: In 20 patients receiving FMT + dual ICI
key_findings.finding: Safety: Grade 1-2 immune-related adverse events (irAEs) occurred in 80% of patients; 65% developed grade >3 irAEs, with diarrhea/colitis being the most frequent grade 3 event (20%). Two patients developed myocarditis (grade 3 and 4). 30% completed all 4 cycles.

key_findings.conditions: In 20 patients receiving FMT + dual ICI
key_findings.finding: Efficacy: Objective Response Rate (ORR) was 70% (2 complete responses, 12 partial responses). Two deaths occurred (one unknown cause, one disease progression).
Beta-diversity analysis showed separate clustering of responders (R) and non-responders (NR) (p=0.024). Responders showed enrichment of Prevotella copri, Ruminoccocaceae, and Eubacterium.
Patients who developed colitis had significantly higher plasma sST2 levels (epithelial integrity marker) one week after FMT compared to those who did not (p<0.05).

Mice treated with feces from human responders (post-FMT) showed reduced tumor growth compared to those treated with non-responder feces. Dual ICI significantly improved tumor control in mice treated with responder feces (p<0.005).

problem_or_question: Whether FMT can be used safely in combination with anti-PD-1/anti-CTLA-4 (dual ICI) therapy and what impact this combination has on the microbiome composition and clinical outcomes in previously untreated advanced melanoma patients.
research_scope: Previously untreated patients with advanced cutaneous melanoma; healthy donors for fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT); avatar mouse models (MCA-205 and B16 OVA).
work_summary: This study reports the results of the FMT-LUMINate trial, a Phase II clinical investigation evaluating the safety and efficacy of combining fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from healthy donors with dual immune checkpoint inhibitors (ipilimumab and nivolumab) in patients with advanced melanoma. The research aimed to determine if FMT could be safely administered alongside dual ICI and to assess its impact on treatment response and the gut microbiome composition. The study included 20 patients who received oral capsule FMT prior to starting dual ICI. Safety was the primary endpoint, while objective response rate (ORR) and microbiome shifts were secondary endpoints. Additionally, longitudinal serum markers of epithelial integrity (sST2) were measured, and stool samples from patients were transplanted into avatar mice to evaluate tumor growth responses under different conditions.
